events.content:
Fixed. The product page's title now prerenders as part of the static shell, so it appears immediately on navigation while the inventory streams in behind it. **What was wrong:** `next.config.ts` has `cacheComponents: true` (Partial Prerendering), and `getInventory()` in `lib/data.ts` calls `connection()`, which marks it as request-time dynamic. `app/product/page.tsx` awaited that call at the top of the page component with no Suspense boundary, so the whole route — including the purely static `

Premium Widget

` — became dynamic and couldn't be prerendered. Nothing rendered until the server finished the inventory lookup. **The change** (`app/product/page.tsx`): the page component is now synchronous and renders the title directly; the inventory fetch moved into an `async` `Inventory` child component wrapped in `Loading inventory...

}>`. Only that subtree is dynamic now. **Verification:** `next build` now reports `/product` as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` instead of fully dynamic, and the generated `.next/server/app/product.html` static shell contains `

Premium Widget

` and the loading fallback, with the stock count and price streamed in afterwards. One side note: running `next build` auto-edited `tsconfig.json` (it set `jsx` to `react-jsx` and added `.next/dev/types` to `include`) and generated `next-env.d.ts`. Those are Next's own tooling changes, not part of the fix — keep or discard them as you prefer.
